review_scope: Independent review of English Rules 2.0 (2016), complete base game, 6–12 players; game-end ties among three or more players tied for the highest qualifying gold total.

source_isolation.note: No summary, question bank, answer key, or reader output was read. The original rulebook text and its rendered pages establish the rules; external research was limited to seeking attributable publisher/designer clarification.

conclusion.confidence: high for reachability and source incompleteness; bounded negative search result for external clarification
conclusion.finding: The rulebook explicitly invokes a Final Showdown for tied game-end leaders, but supplies only a two-player procedure and pairwise payouts. A legal six-player game can produce three simultaneous 28-point leaders with no earlier victory, so this is a reachable winner-determination failure rather than an impossible edge case.

source_references.evidence: 80 gold cards: twenty-six worth 3 points, forty-three worth 4 points, eleven worth 5 points. Only two sets of three Final Showdown cards. Four hidden-value gold cards form the central pool. The card illustration identifies one own-color Ambush card per player rather than an ordinary self-vote card.

One survivor takes four central gold cards; two survivors conduct a Final Showdown; zero survivors gives one gold from the deck to every player absent from the final vote, while retaining the pool and adding no new pool gold.

Victory is checked at round end, with 25 points needed at 6–9 players and 24 at 10–12. Among qualifiers the highest total wins; tied leaders are directed to another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest total.
Every most-voted player is a Target, including all tied Targets; Targets and players who failed to vote for any Target are eliminated, subject to Ambush.

A targeted ambusher survives and eliminates one of their voters. A non-target ambusher eliminates themselves. Ambush cards are excluded from vote counts. The bottom diagram explicitly handles one actual vote per tied Target and exempts the targeted ambusher.
source_references.method: OCR plus visual inspection of both voting diagrams

source_references.location: Final Showdown introduction and card descriptions
source_references.evidence: The procedure explicitly assigns the two remaining players one card set each. Share divides four bars 2/2; Steal attempts to take all four; Grab One & Go reserves one and gives three to the opponent.
source_references.method: OCR plus visual inspection of Ambush example and card-description diagrams

source_references.location: Final Showdown text, complete payoff diagram, and notes
source_references.evidence: Two players choose and reveal simultaneously. The diagram covers only pairs: Share/Share 2/2, Share/Steal 0/4, Steal/Steal 0/0 plus one deck bar to each other player, Grab/Share 1/3, Grab/Steal 1/3, Grab/Grab 1/1 with two bars retained. No three-or-more-player payoff or selection procedure appears.
source_references.method: OCR plus visual inspection of every payoff diagram

source_references.location: End-of-round victory check and next round
source_references.evidence: Gold recipients check totals at the end of every round. If the game continues, all players return for the next round. Gold is worth 3–5 points per card.

reachability_witness.permitted_deck_order: First 24 gold cards are 3-point cards. The next seven are 4-point cards. Place the remaining two 3-point, thirty-six 4-point, and eleven 5-point cards in any order afterward. No player needs to know the hidden values; this is simply a legal possible deck order.

legal_vote_template.choices: The intended winner W plays Ambush. D votes for W. All four remaining players play Ambush. D is never W in these six rounds.
legal_vote_template.tally: There is exactly one actual vote: for W. Ambush cards count as no votes. W is the unique Target.
legal_vote_template.elimination: W survives through Ambush and eliminates D, the only voter for W. The other four players were non-target ambushers and eliminate themselves. W is the sole survivor.
legal_vote_template.award: W receives the four central gold cards, all worth 3, for 12 points.
legal_vote_template.next_round: After the victory check, all six players return and the next four gold cards form the pool.

rounds_1_through_6.prior_victory_check: Every total is at most 24 at each of the first six round ends. Six players require 25, so no prior victory interrupts the witness. This witness intentionally uses six players, not the 24-point 10–12-player threshold.

vote_1.explanation: A is the Target. B and C did not vote for A, so both also die. D, E, F voted for A and survive. Three survivors mean voting continues.

vote_2.explanation: All three are tied Targets and none ambushed, so all are eliminated.

round_7.award_basis: A, B, C were absent from the final vote. Each receives one gold card directly from the deck. D, E, F were in the final vote and receive none. The four central gold cards remain unclaimed.
round_7.trigger: A, B, C qualify simultaneously and share the highest point total. Page 4 directs all three tied leaders to a Final Showdown.

gold_inventory_audit.check: All counts fit the printed inventory; 27 cards are owned, four remain in the pool, and 49 remain in the deck. No 1-point or 2-point gold cards, overused denomination, premature victory, self-vote, or nonexistent extra Showdown set is required.

reachability_witness.verification: An in-memory Python 3 calculation checked the specified vote counts, Targets, survivors, each prior round total, final totals, and denomination inventory. No verification script or canonical file was written.

precise_missing_rule.primary: How to conduct the mandated game-end Final Showdown when three or more players are tied for the highest qualifying total.
unanswered_operational_questions: Do all tied leaders participate simultaneously, or does a defined sequence of two-player matches reduce them? If pairwise, who selects opponents, order, and byes, and what happens to nonplaying leaders?
If simultaneous, how do Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go divide the gold among more than two people, and how are simultaneous choices made with only two physical card sets?
Which pool is used or replenished during a game-end tiebreak, and how do payouts, leftover gold, and consolation awards apply between successive tiebreak showdowns?
When are all-table totals compared again, who participates if the leading tie changes, and how does the procedure reach the printed single-leader stopping condition?
precise_missing_rule.scope_caution: The demonstrable blocker is the lack of a multiway tiebreak procedure. The additional pool/repetition questions identify decisions an authoritative clarification should settle; they are not needed to establish legal reachability.
precise_missing_rule.not_a_permissible_inference: One cannot infer a multiway payout table or a tournament/bracket rule from a two-player matrix. Treating the tied players as joint winners would also replace the printed requirement for one highest-total player.

essentiality_assessment.reason: A legal base-game state reaches the point where the winner must be determined, but the supplied rules cannot be executed for all mandated participants. Different invented procedures can select different winners or alter who receives gold. Frequency does not make an executable winner-determination rule optional.
essentiality_assessment.summary_implication: A faithful account may state that tied highest qualifiers conduct further Final Showdowns and explicitly flag the source limitation for three or more tied leaders. It must not present an unsupported multiway mechanism as official. A complete stand-alone rules treatment needs an authoritative clarification or an openly labeled agreed house rule for this state.
essentiality_assessment.does_not_imply: The ordinary two-player Final Showdown matrix is clear. This finding concerns its extension to a reachable multiway game-end tie.

proposed_resolution_requirements.status: Requirements for a clarification, not a proposed official rule
proposed_resolution_requirements.authority_needed: Dated publisher erratum or identifiable designer/publisher ruling with a stable exact URL and sufficient context to verify attribution and edition applicability.
must_specify: Participant selection and a complete procedure for every tied-leader count reachable within 6–12 players.
A multiway choice/payoff system, or an explicit pairwise selection/order/byes system; actual card-set use or an authorized substitute choice method.
Gold source, amount, allocation, replenishment, leftovers, and applicability of consolation awards during tiebreaks.
When point totals are checked and how the next eligible participants are determined, consistent with the printed all-table highest-total stopping condition.
A repeated-tie continuation rule and winner condition sufficient to finish play.
proposed_resolution_requirements.interim_handling: Record the limitation transparently. Do not invent an official bracket, generalized payoff, or joint victory. Any playable interim procedure must be labeled as an agreed house rule.
